page: Microsoft Azure EC8ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on AMD EPYC 9V74 hardware running under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance provisions 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical x86_64 cores using two hardware threads per core. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Cryptographic processing is accelerated via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets, accompanied by standard AVX, BMI2, and FMA vector extensions, though AVX-512 extensions are absent. Memory provisioning is substantial, offering 64.0 GB of RAM at a consistent ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU.

Storage is addressed by an integrated 322 GB local solid-state drive (SSD), providing low-latency temporary storage for paging, scratch operations, and ephemeral storage pools. GPU acceleration is not present in this instance tier. In compute and system performance benchmarks, the configuration demonstrates stable middle-tier results. CPU evaluations show a stress-ng multi-core score of 7924.17 and a single-core score of 1990.05. Geekbench testing yields a multi-core score of 4751.0 and a single-core score of 1236.0, alongside specialized ratings such as 6392.0 in Clang compilation and 7216.0 in ray tracing.

For data processing and memory tasks, the instance achieves a PassMark memory score of 1998.22 and handles database operations at 2966.91 points. In-memory data manipulation reaches 6.84 million SET operations per second in Redis tests. From a resource efficiency perspective, the high memory-to-vCPU allocation delivers cost-effective density for applications limited primarily by RAM capacity rather than raw compute scaling. The primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of AVX-512 and GPU hardware, which precludes intensive deep learning workloads. As configured, the instance fits production relational databases, Redis caching layers, intermediate ETL operations, and business intelligence reporting systems.
description: Microsoft Azure EC8ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine engineered for memory-intensive enterprise tasks. Powered by AMD EPYC 9V74 x86_64 processors, this instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled, supported by 32 MB of L3 cache. It delivers 64.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a generous 1:8 core-to-memory ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage capabilities include a bundled 322 GB local SSD for high-speed temporary caching and scratch data, while GPU acceleration is omitted. Benchmark testing places the instance solidly in the mid-range performance category across standard workloads, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 4751.0, a PassMark CPU score of 9167.17, and Redis throughput reaching 6.84 million SET operations per second. Its hardware configuration ensures dependable resource density and cost efficiency for production systems. The instance is well suited for relational databases, in-memory caches, data analytics, and intermediate ETL processing pipelines.
